title: Your Engine Explodes Thousands of Times a Minute
sources: Britannica 'Four-stroke cycle' / NASA Glenn Research Center 'Four Stroke Internal Combustion Engine' (grc.nasa.gov engopt) / Haynes 'What is a four-stroke engine' / University of Windsor engine manual 'Four Stroke Cycle Engines': the four strokes are intake (fuel-air mixture drawn in), compression, power (the spark plug ignites the mixture and the burning gas drives the piston down) and exhaust; each cylinder makes one power stroke every two revolutions of the crankshaft

Britannica 'Gasoline engine: camshaft, valves, pistons' / Wikipedia 'Camshaft' / SlashGear 'Crankshaft vs. Camshaft': the connecting rod and crankshaft turn the piston's up-and-down motion into rotation; the camshaft, driven by the crankshaft at half its speed, opens and closes the intake and exhaust valves at the right moments

HowStuffWorks 'What Is an Internal Combustion Engine?' / Capital One 'Car Engines Explained: Cylinders, Layouts' / Explain That Stuff 'Car engines': most car engines have four or more cylinders whose power strokes are spread out (firing order) so the engine runs smoothly; the fuel burns inside the engine itself, hence 'internal combustion'

Arithmetic from the four-stroke facts above: a four-cylinder engine at 3,000 rpm makes 4 x 3,000 / 2 = 6,000 power strokes a minute = 100 per second; at 2,000 rpm it is 4,000 a minute (thousands a minute)

lines.text: Your car's engine sets off thousands of explosions a minute, on purpose.
lines.caps: Your car's engine | sets off thousands | of explosions a minute, | on purpose.

lines.text: If you light gasoline in the open, you just get a fire.
lines.caps: If you light gasoline | in the open, | you just get a fire.

lines.text: So, you trap a puff of fuel and air inside a steel tube, called a cylinder.
lines.caps: So, you trap a puff | of fuel and air | inside a steel tube, | called a cylinder.

lines.text: A spark plug lights it, and the blast shoves a piston down.
lines.caps: A spark plug lights it, | and the blast | shoves a piston down.

lines.text: But a piston only goes up and down, and wheels need to spin.
lines.caps: But a piston only | goes up and down, | and wheels need to spin.

lines.text: So, a rod links it to a crankshaft, like your legs on bike pedals.
lines.caps: So, a rod links it | to a crankshaft, | like your legs | on bike pedals.

lines.text: But after one bang, the cylinder is full of burnt gas.
lines.caps: But after one bang, | the cylinder is full | of burnt gas.

lines.text: So, it works in four strokes: suck in, squeeze, bang, blow out.
lines.caps: So, it works | in four strokes: | suck in, squeeze, | bang, blow out.

lines.text: Valves open and close right on time, pushed by a spinning camshaft.
lines.caps: Valves open and close | right on time, | pushed by a spinning camshaft.

lines.text: But one cylinder only fires every second turn, so it shakes.
lines.caps: But one cylinder only fires | every second turn, | so it shakes.

lines.text: So, most cars use four or more cylinders, taking turns.
lines.caps: So, most cars use | four or more cylinders, | taking turns.

lines.text: At three thousand R P M, a four-cylinder fires a hundred times a second.
lines.caps: At 3,000 RPM, | a four-cylinder fires | 100 times a second.

lines.text: You see, it's tiny explosions, perfectly timed and turned into spin.
lines.caps: You see, it's tiny explosions, | perfectly timed | and turned into spin.

lines.text: That's why it's called internal combustion: the fire happens inside.
lines.caps: That's why it's called | internal combustion: | the fire happens inside.
